Applied AI research
Threshold-conditioned LLM abstention | MSc dissertation
Mar – Sep 2026 · Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face, LoRA
Developed self-sampled confidence training with one LoRA adapter per model, allowing a prompt threshold to control answering versus abstention across Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B.
Evaluated on 500 held-out TriviaQA questions. For tuned Mistral, raising the threshold from 0 to 0.9 reduced incorrect answers from 146 to 15, while answer coverage fell from 97.8% to 42.6%.
Analysed the accuracy–coverage trade-off with paired tests; a separate SimpleQA evaluation exposed near-total abstention at higher thresholds, defining a limit to generalisation.
Related research: sole-author manuscript, “Diagnosis of Reward-Based Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models” (2026).

projects.title: Knowing when not to answer
projects.subtitle: Threshold-conditioned LLM abstention
projects.question: Can one tuned language model change how readily it answers, without retraining for each threshold?
projects.contribution: Designed a threshold-conditioned training and evaluation pipeline using self-sampled confidence and one LoRA adapter per model.
projects.implementation: Studied Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B on TriviaQA, with a separate Mistral evaluation on SimpleQA. A prompt threshold controls the answer/abstain decision.
projects.evidence: The dissertation reports four threshold settings per model on 500 held-out TriviaQA questions. For tuned Mistral, threshold 0 to 0.9 changes incorrect answers from 146 to 15 and coverage from 97.8% to 42.6%.
projects.limits: These are reported experiments, not live inference or independently rerun benchmarks. Lower error comes with fewer answers. The SimpleQA test largely collapsed into abstention at high thresholds; results use one split and training seed.

projects.title: Software for a shared space
projects.subtitle: Community-centre booking application
projects.question: How can a booking move from a visitor's request to an administrator's decision with explicit validation and state changes?
projects.contribution: Built and iterated the booking application, including validation, administrator workflows, scheduled jobs and automated checks. The repository documents AI-assisted development with Claude Code.
projects.implementation: React frontend, Flask API and PostgreSQL storage; approval flows, automatic declines and data-retention jobs. Backend/frontend tests, linting and container builds run in GitHub Actions.
projects.evidence: Current repository code and passing CI include tests against a fresh PostgreSQL database, making this a useful example of engineering beyond a visual prototype.
projects.limits: A project in development. The README still identifies placeholder centre details and log-only email. No claim of live bookings or client adoption.

projects.title: Looking inside a prediction
projects.subtitle: Chest X-ray classification
projects.question: How does a compact CNN compare with transfer learning, and what can interpretation tools reveal about model behaviour?
projects.contribution: Implemented a binary classification pipeline comparing a custom four-block CNN with VGG16 transfer learning and two-phase fine-tuning.
projects.implementation: Compared training approaches and added Grad-CAM image-region attribution and SHAP explanations of engineered features.
projects.evidence: The repository and accompanying report include the model configurations, evaluation and interpretability work.
projects.limits: An academic image-classification study, not a clinically validated diagnostic tool. Attribution visualisations do not establish medical correctness or causal explanations.

projects.title: Below the abstraction
projects.subtitle: 32-bit RISC-V simulator
projects.question: What happens between an instruction entering a processor and the machine state changing?
projects.contribution: Contributed to a four-person simulator project spanning execution, pipelining, caches and a graphical interface.
projects.implementation: Single-cycle and pipelined execution modes with instruction/data caches and a Python GUI for inspecting processor state.
projects.evidence: The repository contains staged implementations and design documentation across the simulator's development phases.
projects.limits: An educational simulator produced by a team. A portfolio diagram is an explanation, not an emulator running the original C/C++ code in the browser.

projects.title: When accuracy hides the problem
projects.subtitle: Diabetes risk classification
projects.question: What does a high overall accuracy hide when minority classes are the ones that matter?
projects.contribution: Compared supervised classifiers for healthy, pre-diabetic and diabetic classes, with exploratory clustering as a separate analysis.
projects.implementation: Examined class imbalance through per-class recall and confusion matrices, comparing methods including logistic regression, SVM, random forest and XGBoost.
projects.evidence: Reported XGBoost results show approximately 83% overall accuracy alongside 40% diabetes recall and 0% prediabetes recall—a clear reason to inspect more than accuracy.
projects.limits: Survey-data coursework, not clinical records or a validated screening system. The class-recall failure is retained rather than presented as a successful diagnostic result.
